intro.text:
Cold air flows through a long, narrow channel with hot walls.

How quickly does the air warm up?

outro.text:
Heat in = heat carried out: the 15 °C rise matches the energy balance to within 0.1 %.

OpenFOAM buoyantSimpleFoam · 2D RANS

captions.text: Air at 27 °C flows in from the left. Both walls are held at 77 °C.
Heat soaks in from the walls, so a warm layer grows along each one.
The hot walls pass on most heat near the inlet, where the air touching them is still cold.
Further along, the warm layers thicken and the cold core in the middle shrinks.
The whole 2 m channel: by the outlet the air is about 15 °C warmer on average.
